input: A defect-reduction project carried out on a moulding cell succeeded in cutting the reject rate from 4.3% to 2.9% over the course of one quarter, which represents a reduction of 1.4 percentage points. The reject rate is the share of moulded units that are rejected at inspection, so the reduction should be understood as a fall in that share rather than a fall in production volume. At a volume of 120k units per year, the lower rate avoids approximately 1680 rejected units per year. It is worth noting that the avoided figure is obtained by multiplying the annual volume by the rate reduction, and it therefore holds only for as long as the improved rate is maintained; a return to the earlier rate would bring the rejected count back with it. The quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and the rates have not been adjusted to account for it. Output lost to the shutdown therefore sits inside the quarter's figures on exactly the same basis as the running production, and the comparison between the two rates is a comparison of unadjusted rates over a quarter that was not a full production quarter. Overall, the reduction is established for that one quarter, and reject performance over a longer period, or in a quarter without a planned shutdown, was not reported.

On the figures given, the project has changed the rate at which the cell produces rejects; whether the change came from the moulding conditions, the tooling or the inspection standard is not stated, and the annual saving figure inherits the basis of the quarter it was measured in.
